readings.subsection: Joshua Blesses Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh
readings.title: Commendation and Dismissal
readings.subtitle: Joshua Sends the Eastern Tribes Home
readings.text:
[Joshua 22:1] Then Yehoshua called for the Re’uḇěnites, and the Gaḏites, and half the tribe of Menashsheh,
[2] and said to them, “You, you have guarded <dn>את</dn> all that Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded you, and have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you.
[3] “You have not left <dn>את</dn> your brothers these many days, up to this day, but have guarded <dn>את</dn> the Charge, the command of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[4] “And now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given rest to your brothers, as <dn>He</dn> promised them. So now, return and go to your tents and to the land of your possession, which Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave you beyond the Yarděn.
[5] “Only, diligently guard to do <dn>את</dn> the command and <dn>את</dn> the Torah which Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded you, to love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and to walk in all <dn>His</dn> ways, and to guard <dn>His</dn> commands, and to cling to <dn>Him</dn>, and to serve <dn>Him</dn> with all your heart and with all your being.”
[6] And Yehoshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.
[7] And to half the tribe of Menashsheh Mosheh had given a possession in Bashan, but to the other half of it Yehoshua gave land among their brothers beyond the Yarděn, westward. So when Yehoshua sent them away to their tents, he also blessed them,
[8] and spoke to them, saying, “Return to your tents with great riches, and with very much livestock, and with silver, and with gold, and with bronze, and with iron, and with countless garments. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers.”
[9] And the children of Re’uḇěn, and the children of Gaḏ, and half the tribe of Menashsheh returned, and left <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl at Shiloh, which is in the land of Kena‛an, to go to the land of Gil‛aḏ, to the land of their possession, which they possessed according to the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by the hand of Mosheh.

readings.title: The Conspicuous Altar
readings.subtitle: Israel Prepares for War Against Their Brothers
readings.text:
[Joshua 22:10] And they came to the districts of the Yarděn which is in the land of Kena‛an, and the children of Re’uḇěn, and the children of Gaḏ, and half the tribe of Menashsheh built a slaughter-place there by the Yarděn, a great conspicuous slaughter-place.
[11] And the children of Yisra’ěl heard it said, “See, the children of Re’uḇěn, and the children of Gaḏ, and half the tribe of Menashsheh have built <dn>את</dn> a slaughter-place opposite the land of Kena‛an, in the districts of the Yarděn, at the border of the children of Yisra’ěl.”
[12] And when the children of Yisra’ěl heard, all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl assembled at Shiloh to go to fight against them.
[13] So the children of Yisra’ěl sent Pineḥas son of El‛azar the priest to the children of Re’uḇěn, and to the children of Gaḏ, and to half the tribe of Menashsheh, into the land of Gil‛aḏ,
[14] and ten rulers with <dn>את</dn> him, one ruler each from the chief house of every tribe of Yisra’ěl. And each one was the head of the house of his father among the divisions of Yisra’ěl.
[15] And they came to the children of Re’uḇěn and to the children of Gaḏ, and to half the tribe of Menashsheh, to the land of Gil‛aḏ, and spoke with <dn>את</dn> them, saying,
[16] “Thus says all the congregation of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘What is this trespass you have committed against the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, to turn away this day from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in that you have built for yourselves a slaughter-place, to rebel against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> this day?
[17] Is <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of Pe‛or not enough for us, from which we have not been cleansed till this day, although there was a plague in the congregation of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,
[18] that you turn away today from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? And it shall be, if you rebel today against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that tomorrow <dn>He</dn> is wroth with all the congregation of Yisra’ěl.
[19] And indeed, if the land of your possession is unclean, then pass over to the land of the possession of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, where the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> dwells, and take possession among us. But do not rebel against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor rebel against us, by building yourselves a slaughter-place besides the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[20] Did not Aḵan son of Zeraḥ commit a trespass in that which is under the ban, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Yisra’ěl? And he was not the only one to die in his crookedness.’ ”

readings.title: The Defense of the Eastern Tribes
readings.subtitle: A Witness, Not for Sacrifice
readings.text:
[Joshua 22:21] Then the children of Re’uḇěn, and the children of Gaḏ, and half the tribe of Menashsheh answered and said to the heads of the divisions of Yisra’ěl,
[22] "<dn>Ěl</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>Ěl</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> knows, and let Yisra’ěl itself know. If this has been in rebellion, or if in trespass against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do not save us this day.
[23] “If we have built ourselves a slaughter-place to turn from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, or if to offer ascending offerings or grain offerings on it, or if to make slaughterings of peace offerings on it, let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> require it.
[24] “But truly, from fear, for a reason we did this, saying, ‘In time to come your sons might speak to our sons, saying, “What have you to do with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl?
[25] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made the Yarděn a border between you and us, you children of Re’uḇěn and children of Gaḏ. You have no portion with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” So your sons would make <dn>את</dn> our sons stop fearing <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’
[26] “So we said, ‘Let us now prepare to build ourselves a slaughter-place, not for ascending offering nor for slaughtering,
[27] but to be a witness between you and us and our generations after us, to do <dn>את</dn> the service of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before <dn>Him</dn> with our ascending offerings, with our slaughterings, and with our peace offerings, that your sons should not say to our sons in time to come, “You have no portion with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” ’
[28] “So we said that it shall be, when they say this to us or to our generations in time to come, that we shall say, ‘See <dn>את</dn> the pattern of the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which our fathers made, though not for ascending offerings nor for slaughterings, but it is a witness between you and us.’
[29] “Far be it from us to rebel against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and to turn from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> this day, to build a slaughter-place for ascending offerings, for grain offerings, or for slaughterings, besides the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> which is before <dn>His</dn> Dwelling Place.”

readings.title: Peace Restored
readings.subtitle: The Altar Named Witness
readings.text:
[Joshua 22:30] And Pineḥas the priest and the rulers of the congregation, and the heads of the thousands of Yisra’ěl who were with <dn>את</dn> him, heard <dn>את</dn> the words that the children of Re’uḇěn, and the children of Gaḏ, and the children of Menashsheh spoke, and it was good in their eyes.
[31] And Pineḥas son of El‛azar the priest said to the children of Re’uḇěn, and to the children of Gaḏ, and to the children of Menashsheh, “Today we know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in our midst, because you have not committed against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> this trespass. Now you have delivered <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl out of the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
[32] And Pineḥas son of El‛azar the priest, and the rulers, returned from the children of Re’uḇěn and the children of Gaḏ, from the land of Gil‛aḏ to the land of Kena‛an, to the children of Yisra’ěl, and brought back word to them.
[33] So the matter was good in the eyes of the children of Yisra’ěl, and the children of Yisra’ěl blessed <dn>Elohim</dn>. And they spoke no more of going against to fight, to destroy <dn>את</dn> the land where the children of Re’uḇěn and Gaḏ dwelt.
[34] And the children of Re’uḇěn and the children of Gaḏ called the slaughter-place, “A witness between us that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn>.”

readings.title: Cling to YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Warnings Against Idolatry and Intermarriage
readings.text:
[Joshua 23:1] And it came to be, a long time after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had given rest to Yisra’ěl from all their enemies round about, that Yehoshua was old, advanced in years.
[2] And Yehoshua called for all Yisra’ěl, and for their elders, and for their heads, and for their judges, and for their officers, and said to them, “I am old, advanced in years.
[3] “And you, you have seen <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has done to all these nations because of you, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who was fighting for you.
[4] “See, I have divided to you by lot <dn>את</dn> these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes, from the Yarděn, with all the nations that I have cut off, as far as the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun.
[5] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> thrust them out from before you, and shall drive <dn>את</dn> them out from before you, and you shall possess <dn>את</dn> their land, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has promised you.
[6] “And you shall be very strong to guard and to do <dn>את</dn> all that is written in the Book of the Torah of Mosheh, so as not to turn aside from it right or left,
[7] so as not to go in among these nations, these who remain among you. And make no mention of the name of their mighty ones, nor swear by them, nor serve them nor bow down to them.
[8] “But cling to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as you have done to this day.
[9] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has driven out from before you great and strong nations. As for you, no one has stood against you to this day.
[10] “One man of you put a thousand to flight, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who is fighting for you, as <dn>He</dn> has promised you.
[11] “And you shall diligently guard yourselves, to love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[12] “But if you do turn back at all, and cling to the remnant of these nations, these that remain among you, and intermarry with them, and go in to them and they to you,
[13] know for certain that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall no longer drive <dn>את</dn> these nations out from before you. And they shall be snares and traps to you, and a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you.
[14] “And see, this day I am going the way of all the earth. And you know in all your hearts and in all your beings that not one word has failed of all the good words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke concerning you. All of it has come to you, and not one word of them has failed.
[15] “And it shall be, that as every good word has come upon you which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> promised you, so <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does bring upon you <dn>את</dn> every evil word, until <dn>He</dn> has destroyed <dn>את</dn> you from this good land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you,
[16] when you transgress <dn>את</dn> the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> commanded you, and shall go and serve other mighty ones, and bow down to them. And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall burn against you, and you shall perish quickly from the good land which <dn>He</dn> has given you.”

readings.title: From Terah to the Promised Land
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Recounts His Faithfulness
readings.text:
[Joshua 24:1] And Yehoshua gathered <dn>את</dn> all the tribes of Yisra’ěl to Sheḵem and called for the elders of Yisra’ěl, and for their heads, and for their judges, and for their officers. And they presented themselves before <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[2] And Yehoshua said to all the people, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘Long ago your fathers dwelt beyond the River – Teraḥ, the father of Aḇraham and the father of Naḥor. And they served other mighty ones.</dq>
[3] <dq>So <dn>I</dn> took <dn>את</dn> your father <dn>את</dn> Aḇraham from beyond the River, and caused him to go through all the land of Kena‛an, and multiplied <dn>את</dn> his offspring and gave him <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq.</dq>
[4] <dq>And to Yitsḥaq <dn>I</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ and <dn>את</dn> Ěsav. And to Ěsav <dn>I</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> the mountains of Sě‛ir to possess, but Ya‛aqoḇ and his children went down to Mitsrayim.</dq>
[5] <dq>Then <dn>I</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> Mosheh and <dn>את</dn> Aharon, and plagued <dn>את</dn> Mitsrayim, as <dn>I</dn> did in their midst. And afterward <dn>I</dn> brought you out.</dq>
[6] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> your fathers out of Mitsrayim, and you came to the sea. And the Mitsrians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.</dq>
[7] <dq>And they cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> put thick darkness between you and the Mitsrians, and brought the sea upon them, and covered them. And your eyes saw <dn>את</dn> what <dn>I</dn> did in Mitsrayim. And you dwelt in the wilderness a long time.</dq>
[8] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> you into the land of the Amorites, who dwelt beyond the Yarděn, and they fought with <dn>את</dn> you. But <dn>I</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> them into your hand, and you possessed <dn>את</dn> their land, and <dn>I</dn> destroyed them from before you.</dq>
[9] <dq>And Balaq son of Tsippor, sovereign of Mo’aḇ, rose up and fought against Yisra’ěl, and sent and called for Bil‛am son of Be‛or to curse <dn>את</dn> you.</dq>
[10] <dq>But <dn>I</dn> refused to listen to Bil‛am, so he continued to bless <dn>את</dn> you, and <dn>I</dn> delivered <dn>את</dn> you out of his hand.</dq>
[11] <dq>And you passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn and came to Yeriḥo. And the masters of Yeriḥo, the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Kena‛anite, and the Ḥittite, and the Girgashite, and the Ḥivvite, and the Yeḇusite fought against you. But <dn>I</dn> gave them into your hand.</dq>
[12] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> sent the hornet before you which drove <dn>את</dn> them out from before you, also the two sovereigns of the Amorites, but not with your sword or with your bow.</dq>
[13] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> gave you a land for which you did not labour, and cities which you did not build. And you dwell in them, you eat of the vineyards and olive-trees which you did not plant.’</dq>

readings.title: We Will Serve YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Covenant Renewed and Witness Stone Set
readings.text:
[Joshua 24:14] “And now, fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn> in perfection and in truth, and put away <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones which your fathers served beyond the River and in Mitsrayim, and serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!
[15] “And if it seems evil in your eyes to serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, choose for yourselves this day <dn>את</dn> whom you are going to serve, whether <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell. But I and my house, we serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
[16] And the people answered and said, “Far be it from us to forsake <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to serve other mighty ones,
[17] for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who has brought us and <dn>את</dn> our fathers up out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage, who did those great signs before our eyes, and has guarded us in all the way that we went and among all the people through whom we passed.
[18] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> drove out from before us <dn>את</dn> all the people, even <dn>את</dn> the Amorites who dwelt in the land. We too serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is our <dn>Elohim</dn>.”
[19] Then Yehoshua said to the people, “You are not able to serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is a set-apart <dn>Elohim</dn>, a jealous <dn>Ěl</dn> is <dn>He</dn>. <dn>He</dn> does not bear with your transgression and with your sins,
[20] if you forsake <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and shall serve mighty ones of a stranger. Then <dn>He</dn> shall turn back and do you evil and consume <dn>את</dn> you, after <dn>He</dn> has been good to you.”
[21] And the people said to Yehoshua, “No, but we do serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!”
[22] Then Yehoshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for yourselves, to serve <dn>Him</dn>.” And they said, “Witnesses!”
[23] “And now, put away <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of the stranger which are in your midst, and incline <dn>את</dn> your heart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl.”
[24] And the people said to Yehoshua, “<dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> we serve, and <dn>His</dn> voice we obey.”
[25] And Yehoshua made a covenant with the people that day, and laid on them a law and a right-ruling in Sheḵem.
[26] Then Yehoshua wrote <dn>את</dn> these words in the Book of the Torah of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And he took a large stone, and set it up there under the oak that was by the set-apart place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[27] And Yehoshua said to all the people, “See, this stone is a witness to us, for it has heard <dn>את</dn> all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke to us. And it shall be a witness against you, lest you lie against your <dn>Elohim</dn>.”
[28] Then Yehoshua sent <dn>את</dn> the people away, each to his own inheritance.

readings.title: The Death of Joshua and Eleazar
readings.subtitle: Joseph's Bones Buried in Shechem
readings.text:
[Joshua 24:29] And after these events it came to be that Yehoshua son of Nun, the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, died, one hundred and ten years old.
[30] And they buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath Seraḥ, which is in the mountains of Ephrayim, on the north side of Mount Ga‛ash.
[31] And Yisra’ěl served <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the days of Yehoshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Yehoshua, who had known <dn>את</dn> all the works of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had done for Yisra’ěl.
[32] And <dn>את</dn> the bones of Yosěph, which the children of Yisra’ěl had brought up out of Mitsrayim, they buried at Sheḵem, in the plot of ground which Ya‛aqoḇ had bought from <dn>את</dn> the sons of Ḥamor the father of Sheḵem for one hundred qesitah, and which had become an inheritance of the children of Yosěph.
[33] And El‛azar son of Aharon died, and they buried him in a hill that belonged to Pineḥas his son, which was given to him in the hill country of Ephrayim.
